text.p: The Italian Senate on Wednesday approved the government's 1997 austerity budget.

The package, which is designed to cut 62.5 trillion lire ($41 billion) off next year's projected deficit in a bid to prepare Italy for the launch of the single European Union currency, now passes to the lower house for ratification.
The lower chamber will start its second reading of the bill on Friday and is scheduled to complete the voting by December 23. If it introduces no changes, the budget will become law.

The package was approved by the Senate by 164 votes to none, with the centre-right opposition bloc, led by media mogul Silvio Berlusconi, and the federalist Northern League party boycotting the ballot to protest against the bill.

Opposition parties have criticised Prime Minister Romano Prodi's budget for relying heavily on tax rises. However they support Italy's bid to be a founder member of European monetary and economic union (EMU).

The International Monetary Fund warned earlier this week that further budgetary measures would be needed next year if Italy was to reach one of the key goals laid down in the European Union's Maastricht treaty for countries wishing to join EMU.
